name: Cell detachment and QC module v1 (demo scale)
description: DEMO SCALE: drawn 90 x 50 mm, scaled uniformly by 0.324 into 30 x 20 mm (depths unchanged at 0.15 mm); channels clamped up to 0.2 mm, ports 0.8 mm at >= 5 mm pitch. 4 ports, so no port merges needed. Capability lost: serpentine cut from 90 to ~12 mm, culture area ~10x smaller. The original design notes follow, quoted at the original 90 x 50 mm scale (the 100 um feature floor there is now the 200 um floor): A deliberately SMALL 90 x 50 mm module: it detaches adherent cells enzymatically, neutralises on the way out, and gives a counting window. It does NOT wash, filter, concentrate or exchange buffer, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Those four steps were costed against a bench tube and lost: at a 100 um feature floor, deterministic lateral displacement needs 12-45 um gaps, impedance counting needs a 20-50 um aperture, a pillar gap that removes 30-40 um clumps is impossible, and the final viscous resuspension (roughly two orders of magnitude above water) collapses the Reynolds number by the same factor so inertial focusing stops working altogether. Doing all six steps on chip gives roughly 0.35 cumulative recovery in about 50 min; the two kept here plus a tube give roughly 0.7 in about 30 min. cult_1 is the adherent chamber and the only heated zone; mix_1 is a herringbone mixer (block herringbone_mixer) on a folded path that neutralises by co-flowing quench buffer: diffusion alone across 100 um would take ~100 s, and at Re far below 1 a plain serpentine fold does not mix at all, it only stacks the two streams, so the mixing is done by chaotic advection over chevron relief in the same embossing depth; qc_1 is a plain transparent window, 150 um deep, imaged from outside by a phone or USB microscope. Every feature is >= 100 um, one embossing depth, no photolithography. Geometry is ours; the methods it serves are cited in protocols/cell_prep_v1.json. CELL FILTER BEFORE THE NOZZLE - OFF CHIP, AND NOW DECLARED. This module hands its cells to the encapsulator (pipeline hand-off cellprep_to_module2, out_cells -> in_core), whose nozzle is 300 um. An unfiltered clump wider than that nozzle blocks it and the run ends, and until 7 Nov 2026 this spec declared no filter of any kind, so nothing in the repo could compare a clump size against that nozzle. It now declares cell_filter.gap_um = 30. WHY 30 AND NOT 40. Two nozzles bound it. The pipeline's actual nozzle is 300 um, and contracts/blocks.json retains a particle only while the gap is strictly below trap.gap_factor_high x its diameter, so a gap of g passes everything below g / 0.4 = 2.5 g and protecting a 300 um nozzle needs a gap under 120 um. The second bound is tighter: a chip that declares no encapsulation stage of its own is checked against contracts/parameters.json encapsulation.nozzle_um, the bought kit's 40 x 40 um flow-focusing nozzle, and the check is strict, so the bench step's original 40 um strainer sat exactly ON that nozzle rather than under it. 30 um clears both, is a stock woven nylon mesh size, holds clumps from about 75 um upwards and still passes the 10-20 um single cells this module exists to deliver with room to spare. THAT FILTER IS NOT ON THIS CHIP AND CANNOT BE. The in-plane fabrication floor is 200 um, already above the 120 um the 300 um nozzle needs, so NO printed pillar or mesh gap here can do the job - a 200 um printed gap would hold only clumps of about 500 um and upwards and would wave 300-500 um clumps straight into the nozzle, which is worse than useless because it would look like a filter. The depth-weir trick that rescues retention elsewhere in the fleet does not rescue it either: this chip has one embossing depth of 150 um, so any gap under 120 um means a crest under 30 um tall, and at the roughly +/-20 um z tolerance quoted in blocks.json that crest is +/-67% - it can come out as nothing (no weir) or tall enough to close the channel. A bought mesh clamped in a recessed ledge (blocks.json retention.alternatives_ranked) would work on chip, since the 200 um floor does not apply to a bought part, but it adds a manual assembly step and a ledge this 30 x 20 mm layout has no room for, and the same bought mesh in a tube does the identical job on a path the pipeline already walks. So the filtration is a bought 30 um mesh at the bench, in the tube between out_cells and the encapsulator's core inlet: the spin / strain / resuspend step that out_cells's note and the cellprep_to_module2 hand-off already describe, one mesh size finer than it used to say. The only thing that changed on chip is that the gap is now DATA the checkers read (tools/check_chip_spec.py compares it with both the local and the downstream nozzle) instead of prose. This is consistent with the decision recorded above - this module deliberately does not filter on chip - and it does not widen the module's claim: THE FILTRATION IS OFF CHIP.

chambers.note: Adherent growth area, now about 0.32 cm2 (was 3 cm2), roughly 30k cells at typical density, still about 3x the ~10,000 cells this pipeline consumes. The only heated zone on the board.

Neutralisation mixer, shortened from 90 mm to ~12 mm of folded path to fit the scaled 4.5 x 1.9 mm footprint (0.2 mm lanes, 0.4 mm walls). Residence is about 7x shorter at equal flow, so slow the flow. MIXING HAS TO BE ADVECTIVE, so the block is a herringbone_mixer, NOT a plain serpentine_channel: at Re far below 1 a folded channel only stacks the quench buffer beside the cell stream and then waits on diffusion across the 0.2 mm lane, which is the ~100 s this stage cannot afford. The chevrons are relief in the same 0.15 mm embossing, like a weir crest, so this is still one embossing depth and one fluidic layer, every feature is in plane at or above 0.2 mm, and the lane cross-section is unchanged (the folded path still sets the residence time).

Static counting window, 150 um deep, which is about a haemocytometer's depth. Stopped-flow, imaged from outside. Counting ~400 cells gives a 5% Poisson CV, and a 20% concentration error only moves single-capsule occupancy by about 15%, so this is accurate enough and an in-line counter is not worth building.

ports.note: To a chilled tube. Everything after this is bench: spin, 30 um mesh, resuspend. That mesh is the chip's declared cell_filter (gap_um 30, was written as a 40 um strainer) and it is OFF CHIP by necessity: the encapsulator's nozzle is 300 um, protecting it needs a gap under 120 um, and the in-plane fabrication floor is 200 um. 30 rather than 40 because the bought kit's own nozzle is 40 um and the filter must be strictly finer than the nozzle it feeds. See the description.
